newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - BRITISH BUSINESS - JUNE 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - BRITISH BUSINESS - JUNE 15.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents.
SUNDAY TELEGRAPH
-- RAILTRACK FACES 500M STG WINDFALL TAX

Railtrack could be forced to delay investment plans and cut shareholders' dividends after rumours that the government is planning a introduce a 500m stg windfall tax against it. The government believes the company was sold off too cheaply.
-- WELSH MINERS SUE GERMANS OVER SUBSIDY

Celtic Energy is threatening to sue the German government and Preusag Anthrazit, an offshoot of Veba, over illegal state subsidies which it claims are destroying its market for anthracite coal. The Welsh energy company acquired a series of pits in the privatisation of British Coal.
-- MARCHPOLE GROOMED FOR 130M STG LISTING
Marchpole Group, the London based menswear licensee for Yves Saint Laurent and Jasper Conran brands, is planning to come to the stockmarket. The likely listing value of the company is 130m stg.
-- BA DIRECTORS TAKE PAY CUT

Despite record profits at British Airways, both chief executive, Robert Ayling, and Derek Stevens, chief financial officer, took pay cuts last year. British Airways is currently trying to push through a 1bn stg efficiency programme which includes pay freezes or cuts for 55,000 staff.
-- SMALL FIRMS LOSES 6BN STG TO CRIME

According to a report from the British Chamber of Commerce crime is costing small businesses almost 6bn stg a year. The BCC has called on the Home Secretary to help companies reduce this staggering bill.
SUNDAY TIMES
-- AMERICA'S CHIQUITA GOES BANANAS OVER ALBERT FISHER

US fresh produce group Chiquita Brands is reported to be considering a bid for UK food processing and distribution group Albert Fisher. The company is valued at 335m stg following a statement from chairman Stephen Walls that Fisher had received a bid approach which may or may not lead to an offer.
-- NATWEST IN U-TURN OVER MARKETS

NatWest's chief executive, Derek Wanless, is preparing to abandon the group's plan to turn NatWest Markets into one of the world's 10 largest investment banks. The ban is set to publish a three month investigation into how losses in its options-trading division mounted to 90m stg without being detected.
-- BAe JOINS LOCKHEED TO BATTLE FOR FIGHTER

British Aerospace is to join forces with Lockheed Martin rather than Boeing to bid for the lucrative 130bn stg order for 3,000 Joint Strike Fighters. Under the deal, which followed months of negotiations, BAe may get a 15 percent stake in the American group's bid, including extensive manufacturing work.
-- BRANSON'S RECORD CASH BOOST

McCarthy brothers have given Richard Branson a boost by investing 45m in his new V2 record label. They will buy a 33 percent stake in V2 through their company McCarthy Corporation. Branson will use the cash to buy new talent and stakes in other independent record labels.
-- ABBEY IS UNMASKED AS BIDDER FOR CATER ALLEN

The mysterious bidder for discount house Cater Allen has turned out to be Abbey National. Cater Allen has been in negotiations with an unnamed bidder since the start of the month over a deal worth 200m stg. Cater Allen has a number of small businesses that would fit neatly within Abbey National's portfolio.
THE OBSERVER
-- TREASURY CRACKDOWN ON PENSIONS CHIEFS

The government is to announce plans for a far-reaching review of pension provision next month. Directors of pensions and insurance firms could be disqualified and their companies barred from providing second-tier 'stakeholder pensions' if they fail to clear up the pensions mis-selling scandal.
-- MINISTER SANCTIONS US OWNERSHIP OF BRITISH POWER

City fears of a Monopolies and Mergers Commission investigation into PacifiCorp's 3.7bn stg bid for Energy Group have been reduced after the Energy minister John Battle said he was not against US ownership of regional electricity companies in principle. Meanwhile Entergy Corporation, the US company which recently purchased London Electricity, is to cut a third of its London workforce.
-- MMC MAY FORCE BRITISH GAS TO CUT BILLS BY AT LEAST 20 STG

The long-awaited Monopolies and Mergers Commission report on British Gas, to be published this week, could result in a cut in domestic gas bills of more than 20 stg. Ofgas director general Clare Spottiswoode is likely to claim victory even though her proposals have been trimmed. BG could find it difficult to maintain its dividend with its revenues predicted to fall by up to 400m stg.
-- LORD WEINSTOCK FROWNS ON SIMPSON'S BAe FLIRTATION

Lord Weinstock, honorary chairman of GEC, is believed to be attempting to block managing director George Simpson from trying to explore a link with BAe. The move looks increasingly likely as part of a European defence rationalisation according to one industry source.
-- STAGS STAMPEDE TO NORWICH FLOAT

City forecast are that tomorrow's flotation of Norwich Union will open at more than 350p. However, some investors will not receive their shares certificates until later in the week and many will receive fewer shares than expected after the share offer was heavily oversubscribed.
INDEPENDENT ON SUNDAY
-- INVESTORS INVITED TO SUP AT THE TUP

Pub entrepreneur Hugh Corbett is to bring his Tup Inns chain to the Alternative Investment Market in a bid to raise between 1m stg and 1.5m stg to fund expansion. The float is expected to value the company at between 3.5m stg and 4m stg, based on the company's predicted profits for 1997 of about 350,000 stg after tax.
-- POWER: HERE WE GO AGAIN

US firms Central and South West Corporation and Entergy are thinking about merging their UK electricity businesses and refloating the combined company on the London market. Last week Eastern Group, owners of Eastern Electric, agreed a 3.65bn stg by US PacifiCorp.
-- MONDEX IN THE MONEY

Smart card group Mondex is already making money, even though its pioneering cash cards have not yet been officially issued. The company has reported fee income of 29.4m stg and pre- tax profits of 2.69m stg for July to December 1996, its first period of operation. Mondex is hoping to challenge credit card companies such as Visa with its smart cards, which use computer chips to allow consumers to 'load' the cards with cash and spend it on small items in the same way as with a phone card.
-- 'EURO-BOEING' PLAN FOR AIRBUS

British Aerospace is thought to be proposing a plan for it and Airbus partners Aerospatiale, Dasa and Casa to pool resources, under an independent management team, so its military aerospace businesses could compete more effectively against recently merged Boeing-McDonnell Douglas.
-- JAPAN SCANDAL WIDENS

'Ethical' retailer Body Shop has become embroiled in a corporate racketeering scandal in Japan. The company is linked to the former president of a Japanese supermarket chain who was arrested last week on suspicion of involvement in corporate racketeering. The supermarket chain, Jusco, is the local head franchisee of Body Shop, although Jusco itself has not been implicated in the case.
MAIL ON SUNDAY
-- GRANADA IN MERGER MOVE FOR TV GIANT

Granada Group could mount a full-scale takeover bid for United News & Media, owners of Anglia and Meridian TV and Express Newspapers company, after talks according to industry sources. United's Lord Hollick and Granada's Gerry Robinson have already talked about a jointly held TV company.
-- BROWN'S STAMP DUTY PLANS SHAKE CITY

Jeremy Bayliss, president of the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors, has warned the Chancellor that any increase in stamp duty on property and share deals at a time of increasing interest rates could price many housebuyers out of the fragile house market.
-- NATIONWIDE REFUSES TO LIFE HOME LOAN RATES

The country's biggest building society, Nationwide, is to highlight the benefits of mutuality tomorrow by refusing to raise its mortgage rate after the recent quarter-point base rate rise. However, the building society has been flooded with new investors hoping for windfall shares if they abandon mutual status.
-- LOYALTY LOCK ON COMPUTER STAFF

Scottish Equitable is offering a loyalty bonus of around 15 percent to key computer staff if they stay with the company after the millennium. Standard Life and Scottish Life have already awarded computer staff with rises of between 10 and 15 percent.
-- PFI BOSS HITS AT 100M STG WASTE ON NHS SCHEMES

David Steeds, chief executive of the influential private finance panel executive, said more than 100m stg of taxpayers' money has been wasted on duplicated advice to Private Finance Initiative schemes in the NHS. His figures are three times higher than earlier government estimates.
